summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis of CXCR2, CXCR1 and their ligand CXCL8. CXCR2 ranks first in the deterministic convergence ranking: it is raised in all five biopsy cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa of the same patient, genetically supported in Open Targets and has clinical-stage antagonists, none approved for UC. Single-cell data place almost all CXCR2, CXCR1 and CXCL8 transcripts in neutrophils, and composition adjustment shrinks the CXCR2 change and removes the CXCL8 change, so the axis reads first as a marker of neutrophil influx and only secondarily as a recruitment target.

Candidates that hold up best as tissue-level targets keep a significant change after composition adjustment in a replicated cell of origin: MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts, DUOX2 in enterocytes and IDO1 in myeloid cells. OSMR is the only stromal candidate with both genetic support and a clinical antibody (vixarelimab), but its residual change after adjustment is small. JAK2 is a genetics-led positive control whose expression change is modest.

The most reproducible biomarkers are the loss of epithelial metabolic and barrier genes (CLDN8, HMGCS2, SLC26A2), decreased in all five cohorts, and the gain of neutrophil, antimicrobial and epithelial-stress genes (S100A8, AQP9, CHI3L1, DUOX2). These are markers of inflamed, injured mucosa and of neutrophil infiltration rather than drug targets; the HMGCS2 loss is confined to inflamed mucosa.

At the pathway level JAK-STAT, TNFa and NFkB activity and STAT3 transcription-factor activity are raised in all five cohorts; these axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs and serve as positive controls. In the trial cohorts, baseline TNFa activity and the genes OSM, TREM1, CXCL8 and CXCR2 are higher in ustekinumab non-responders but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders, with null drug-by-placebo interactions where tested, so they mark disease severity rather than drug-specific resistance; the drug targets IL23A and ITGB7 do not stratify response to their own drugs.

Among first-in-class candidates with no clinical drug, SDR16C5 (epithelial, composition-intrinsic, lineage replicated) and CHRDL2 (stromal, replicated, but largely composition-driven and with notable vital-organ RNA) are the most credible hypotheses for experimental validation; LAX1 and ADGRG3 rank high in the screen but reflect plasma-cell and neutrophil influx.

expression.text: Across the five-cohort random-effects meta-analysis, the largest and most reproducible increases in UC mucosa are neutrophil-recruitment, antimicrobial and remodelling genes. The secreted chitinase-like protein CHI3L1 rises by a pooled log2FC of [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.714], the calprotectin subunit S100A8 by [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.647], the epithelial oxidase DUOX2 by [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3213] and the collagenase MMP1 by [gene=MMP1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.661], each in the same direction in all five cohorts. MMP3, MMP7 and MMP10 follow the same pattern, a tissue-remodelling signature, and the epithelial serpin SERPINB5 has the most significant pooled change of the top genes (padj [gene=SERPINB5; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.81e-135]).

The strongest decreases describe a loss of epithelial metabolism and barrier. The tight-junction gene CLDN8 is the most strongly lost gene, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.5181], and the sulfate transporter SLC26A2 falls by [gene=SLC26A2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.496]; both, like the ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2, are decreased in five of five cohorts. Together with the gain of antimicrobial and neutrophil genes, this describes a mucosa that loses colonocyte metabolism and barrier function while recruiting neutrophils; these are biomarkers of epithelial injury, not drug targets.

CXCR2, the top-ranked convergence gene, has a smaller pooled change than the chemokines it binds, log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], but it is raised in all five cohorts. Genes such as JAK2, FCGR2A and IL2RA rank high because of genetics and tractability rather than expression, and between-cohort heterogeneity is high for most top genes, so pooled fold changes describe direction and approximate size only.

inflammation.text: Within the same patients (MSCCR, paired inflamed vs non-inflamed biopsies), the neutrophil and epithelial-defence genes are local to inflamed mucosa: CXCR2 rises by a paired log2FC of [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], CXCR1 by [gene=CXCR1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.193] and CHI3L1 by [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.6182]. The loss of HMGCS2 is equally local, a paired log2FC of [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508], while non-inflamed mucosa is essentially unchanged against controls ([gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]); epithelial metabolic loss therefore accompanies active inflammation rather than preceding it.

A few changes are already present, more weakly, in non-inflamed mucosa. CHI3L1 is modestly raised in non-inflamed mucosa versus controls ([gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8377]), so it carries a disease-level signal beyond the inflamed patch. OSMR, by contrast, is up in inflamed versus paired non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.8848]) but nearly flat in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1755]), a purely local inflammatory change. The non-inflamed contrast exists only in MSCCR, so this separation rests on one cohort.

replication.text: The discovery cohort's leading changes reproduce well in the four microarray cohorts: every gene in the top of the convergence ranking except CCL2 changes in the same direction in all five cohorts. CLDN8 illustrates the pattern, significantly decreased in each cohort, from [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE206285; layer=rna; cohort=GSE206285; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=-5.9822] in UNIFI to a still significant loss in the small Leuven infliximab cohort (padj [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.000467]). Replication is weaker for REG1A, which is not significant in that Leuven cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]), and microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq, so replication is judged on direction and significance.

literature.text: Published support in the verbatim-validated corpus is uneven and mostly bioinformatic or preclinical. CXCL8 signalling through CXCR1 and CXCR2 is linked to UC pathogenesis via PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB and appears as a network hub, and CHI3L1 is reported to promote macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1 and NF-kappaB, with in vitro binding of a repurposed drug. AQP9 is described as a neutrophil gene that promotes neutrophil extracellular traps in mouse colitis, and IDO1 as a driver of M1 macrophage polarisation in a single study with a mouse inhibitor experiment. DUOX2, S100A9, CXCL1, LCN2 and HMGCS2 appear mainly as diagnostic biomarkers.

Two literature signals bear on treatment. In tofacitinib non-responders, macrophages and fibroblasts expanded after treatment with up-regulation of IL1B and other myeloid and stromal genes, and transcripts changed by mirikizumab, including MMP1, MMP3 and S100A8, track endoscopic and histologic indices, supporting their use as pharmacodynamic biomarkers. The corpus is silent where other streams are strong: CXCR2, CXCR1 and CD274 have no extracted literature relations despite genetic and tractability support, and the only CXCR2 corpus mention is as a hub gene of active UC.

external.text: Open Targets separates the candidates into genetics-led and expression-led groups. CXCR2 is the only top-ranked gene with strong biopsy up-regulation, human genetic support (association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345]) and clinical-stage small-molecule antagonists, all in other indications; it is a repurposing candidate, not an approved UC target. JAK2, a known UC target and positive control, has stronger genetic association ([gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) but a modest expression change, and FCGR2A ([gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5543]) and OSMR ([gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3907]) also carry genetic support; only OSMR has a clinical antibody (vixarelimab). Approved UC targets such as TNF and IL23A are absent from the stored ranking because their biopsy expression streams are weak.

The expression-led candidates have no genetic support. CXCL8 is strongly induced but weakly associated ([gene=CXCL8; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1087]) and is targeted only by phase 2 antibodies; IDO1 (linrodostat, epacadostat) and MMP1 (broad-spectrum metalloproteinase inhibitors) have drugs from other indications; CHI3L1, DUOX2 and AQP9 have no drug at all. CD274 is genetically associated, but the approved PD-L1 antibodies block a regulatory brake, the opposite of what UC would need. STRING places CXCR2 among the ELR+ CXC chemokines, a neutrophil-recruitment module shared with CXCL8 and CXCL1.

cells.text: Single-cell data assign the leading neutrophil-axis genes to neutrophils. In the Gubatan dataset, which captured neutrophils, CXCR2 has a neutrophil share of [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts, CXCR1 [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962] and S100A8 [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909], and AQP9 is likewise overwhelmingly neutrophil. Smillie did not capture neutrophils, so its attribution of CXCR2 and CXCR1 to T/NK cells is an artefact that does not replicate. CXCL8 is mixed: macrophages in Smillie (replicated) and neutrophils in Gubatan ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]).

Composition adjustment separates cell influx from tissue change. CXCR2 keeps only a small part of its bulk increase (retained fraction [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]), and CXCL8 loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]); S100A8 partly survives ([gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]), reporting both influx and myeloid activation. These genes are therefore markers of neutrophil infiltration, and any drug against them would act on recruitment. Because lineage scores also rise when resident cells are activated, the adjustment can over-correct, so a lost change is not proof of pure influx.

Other candidates are tissue changes in a replicated cell of origin. MMP1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts (stromal share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]) and stays significant after adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]); DUOX2 is enterocyte-derived (epithelial share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]) with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]; IDO1 is myeloid and largely intrinsic ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]). OSMR is stromal ([gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907]) with a small residual change ([gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.2528]), and CD274 has a mixed plasma-cell, macrophage and neutrophil source with a partly retained change ([gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]). CXCL1, MMP3, MMP7, MMP10, CHI3L1, LCN2 and SERPINB5 were not examined at cell level.

pathways.text: Inferred pathway activity confirms the known drivers of inflamed mucosa. JAK-STAT activity is up in all five cohorts and down in none (for example t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68] in MSCCR), TNFa activity is strongest in UNIFI (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]) with NFkB alongside, and STAT3 transcription-factor activity is up in every cohort (t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0] in UNIFI). These axes are already targeted by approved drugs and act as positive controls. EGFR, MAPK, PI3K, TGFb, VEGF and hypoxia (with HIF1A activity) are also up everywhere, so broad pathway activation does not discriminate between candidates; only p53 and Androgen are inconsistent (p53 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59] in one Leuven cohort).

The most specific cell-cell circuit is a neutrophil loop: CXCL8 from the Neutrophil CXCR4 state to CXCR2 on other neutrophil states rises in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]), and neutrophil CXCL8 to ACKR1 venular endothelium rises too ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]), a plausible recruitment route through an atypical, non-signalling receptor. This axis is untargeted in UC: antagonists of CXCR1 and CXCR2 are clinical-stage in other indications only.

Two other circuits are weaker than they look. IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages pairs with IL1R2 on neutrophil states ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059]), but IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this may reflect IL-1 buffering rather than signalling; IL-1 blockade exists but not in UC. Neutrophil OSM acting on lamina propria fibroblasts through IL6ST scores lower in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa ([type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]), so the neutrophil-OSM-fibroblast hypothesis is not supported as a leading circuit here. All edges are co-expression of ligand and receptor, not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: Baseline pathway activity associated with non-response is shared across drugs and with placebo. TNFa activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]); NFkB is associated with non-response in all four biologic arms, for example infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), and TGFb with ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not golimumab. JAK-STAT does not reach significance for golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]) or vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]). These are severity axes rather than drug-specific resistance mechanisms.

At gene level, OSM (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), TREM1 (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]), CXCL8 (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) and the top convergence gene CXCR2 (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) are higher in ustekinumab non-responders, but CXCR2 also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]) and the drug-by-placebo interaction is null for OSM (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and TREM1 (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.983]); they mark neutrophil-driven severity. The drugs' own targets do not stratify response: IL23A for ustekinumab (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 for vedolizumab (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), the latter in a small arm.

discovery.text: SDR16C5, a short-chain retinol dehydrogenase, is the cleanest first-in-class hypothesis. It rises by a pooled log2FC of [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.552] in UC mucosa, is made by epithelium (share [gene=SDR16C5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.918]) with the lineage replicated in the second dataset, and keeps most of its change after composition adjustment (retained [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.66]). It is predicted antibody-tractable, has no clinical drug and limited vital-organ RNA ([gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=26.9] nTPM). Missing are treatment-response data and any functional evidence that it drives, rather than accompanies, epithelial injury.

CHRDL2, a secreted BMP antagonist, is made by inflammatory fibroblasts (stromal share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]) and the attribution replicates, but most of its bulk rise tracks composition (retained [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]) and it has the highest vital-organ RNA among the top candidates ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM). It is a stromal hypothesis whose safety window and fibroblast-specific effect need testing before it can be considered a target.

Three other screen leaders are weaker. LAX1 is the strongest screen hit but its main inflamed-mucosa source is plasma cells (share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.433]) and the lineage call does not replicate, so its rise reflects immune infiltration. ADGRG3 is the only top candidate with both antibody and small-molecule tractability, but it is almost entirely neutrophil-derived ([gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]). XKR9 is epithelial and intrinsic but up in only a minority of cohorts ([gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2] cohorts), so replication is its main gap.

integration.text: The streams agree most strongly on the neutrophil-recruitment axis and the epithelial-loss signature. CXCR2 and CXCR1 combine replicated expression, local inflammation, genetics and tractability, CXCL8 adds expression and literature, and single-cell data, cell-cell circuits and the trial cohorts all point to neutrophils as the cell carrying the signal. Epithelial barrier and metabolic loss (CLDN8, HMGCS2, SLC26A2) is equally consistent across cohorts and is supported by literature as a diagnostic signature. The established axes JAK-STAT, TNFa and NFkB behave as positive controls in pathway activity, and JAK2 does so through genetics.

The streams disagree on what the top-ranked genes mean. Expression ranks neutrophil genes highest, but composition adjustment shows that much of this is cell influx, so expression rank overstates their value as tissue targets; conversely MMP1, DUOX2 and IDO1 have no genetic support yet are the clearest tissue changes. Genetics favours JAK2, FCGR2A and OSMR, which change modestly in biopsies, and literature is silent on CXCR2, CXCR1 and CD274 despite strong Open Targets support. Finally, baseline levels of the candidate genes predict non-response to ustekinumab and placebo alike, so none is yet a drug-specific response biomarker.

targets.rationale: Rank one in convergence, with all six streams: up in five of five cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa, genetic support and clinical-stage antagonists from other indications. Kept first, but as a target of neutrophil recruitment rather than of resident tissue: transcripts are neutrophil-derived, most of the bulk change is composition, and baseline levels track severity in placebo as well as ustekinumab arms.

Moved above its numeric rank: replicated in five cohorts, made by inflammatory fibroblasts with a replicated attribution, and significant after composition adjustment, so a genuine tissue change. Drug routes are broad-spectrum metalloproteinase inhibitors; it lacks genetic support and is also a pharmacodynamic biomarker of mirikizumab.

Strong, replicated rise that largely survives composition adjustment in myeloid cells, with clinical-stage inhibitors from oncology and preclinical evidence that it drives M1 polarisation. No genetic support, so a repurposing hypothesis.

Below the top of the convergence list but raised here: the only stromal candidate with both genetic support and a clinical antibody (vixarelimab), and its change is local to inflamed mucosa. The residual change after composition adjustment is small, and the neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is not supported, so efficacy is uncertain.

Positive control: a known UC target class (JAK inhibitors) with the strongest genetic association among the candidates and a modest expression change; JAK-STAT and STAT3 activity are up in all cohorts.

Rank three and among the largest pooled increases, but its change loses significance after composition adjustment, genetics is weak and baseline levels track severity in placebo as well as ustekinumab. Best used as a marker of neutrophil and myeloid inflammation; antibodies exist only at phase 2.
Enterocyte-intrinsic change that survives composition adjustment and is local to inflamed mucosa; a strong biomarker of epithelial innate stress, but with low tractability, no drug and no genetics.

The largest replicated increase among top genes, local to inflamed mucosa but also raised in non-inflamed mucosa; literature reports a mechanistic role in macrophage pyroptosis, but there is no drug and no genetics, and its cell source was not examined.
Rank two with genetic support and shared antagonists with CXCR2, but almost entirely neutrophil-expressed and not tested for treatment response, so ranked here as a neutrophil influx marker.

Calprotectin subunit with one of the largest replicated increases; mostly neutrophil-derived with a partly retained change, consistent with its established use as a faecal inflammation marker rather than a target.
Loss of epithelial ketogenesis, down in all five cohorts and confined to inflamed mucosa; a marker of epithelial metabolic failure, not a target.
The most strongly lost gene, significantly decreased in every cohort; a barrier-loss biomarker of mucosal damage.

Exploratory: first-in-class epithelial candidate from the discovery screen, intrinsic after composition adjustment with a replicated lineage and predicted antibody tractability; needs functional and response data.

Exploratory: first-in-class stromal candidate with a replicated fibroblast source, but largely composition-driven and with the highest vital-organ RNA of the top candidates, so safety must be resolved first.

limitations.text: Bulk biopsy expression mixes tissue change with immune infiltration; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so a lost change is not proof of pure influx.

Smillie single-cell data contain no neutrophils, so cell-source calls for neutrophil genes rest on the Gubatan dataset alone; CXCL1, MMP3, MMP7, MMP10, CHI3L1, LCN2 and SERPINB5 were not examined at cell level.
The inflamed versus non-inflamed comparison comes from one cohort (MSCCR); microarray fold changes are compressed and between-cohort heterogeneity is high, so pooled fold changes are approximate.
Ligand-receptor edges are co-expression scores from one dataset and do not prove signalling; ACKR1 and IL1R2 are atypical or decoy receptors.
Treatment-response associations are cross-sectional baseline differences; golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms are small, and CXCR1, CD274, IDO1 and MMP1 were not tested for response.

Literature support is mostly bioinformatic or mouse-based; the PubMed connector was unavailable, and one corpus study reports no association between mucosal expression signatures and anti-TNF response. Drug stages come from Open Targets in any indication and imply no UC efficacy; TNF and IL23A are absent from the stored ranking.
